vulnerabilities: Extreme concentration of central energy processing (Abqaiq facility) and coastal desalination infrastructure — a small number of strikes could cause catastrophic oil-production and water-supply loss simultaneously
Physical export dependence on the Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb chokepoints — all seaborne crude must transit one or the other to reach open ocean
Absence of a domestic high-tech industrial base — high reliance on foreign arms imports exposes Saudi Arabia to legislative embargo risk during regional disputes
Absolute water scarcity — zero permanent rivers, over 60% of potable water needs met via energy-intensive desalination
strengths: Global oil market swing-producer leverage as OPEC+ leader — lowest extraction cost per barrel plus spare capacity to influence global supply
Custodian of Islam's holiest sites (Mecca and Medina), conferring unmatched religious soft power across roughly 1.8 billion Muslims worldwide
Vast sovereign wealth fund (Public Investment Fund) capital deployment across global strategic assets
Geographic span bridging both the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, with coastlines on two major energy chokepoints
Modern Western military hardware arsenal (F-15SA, Eurofighter Typhoon, PAC-3 Patriot, THAAD)
